title: God clothes Adam and Eve — Genesis 3
paragraphs: God clothes Adam and Eve — Genesis 3
He didn’t leave them naked in their shame.

After the fruit.
After the hiding.
After the blame.

Genesis 3 is not just the story of humanity falling. It is the story of God refusing to abandon fallen people. Adam and Eve had sewn fig leaves together, trying to cover what sin had exposed. But human coverings are always thin. Fragile. Temporary. Shame management is not salvation.
Then Genesis 3:21 hits like thunder wrapped in mercy: “And the LORD God made for Adam and for his wife garments of skins and clothed them.”

Not because sin was small.
Not because rebellion was excusable.
But because even in judgment, God was already revealing grace.

Those garments were not random. Something had to die so their shame could be covered. Right there in Eden, through tears and exile, a shadow of the Gospel appears. Innocence laid down. Guilt covered. Mercy provided by God Himself.

God did not say, “Fix yourself first.”
He did not say, “Stitch better leaves.”
He clothed them Himself.
That points us straight to Jesus.

Because the skins in Eden were only a whisper. Christ is the fulfillment. On the cross, Jesus bore our guilt, our nakedness, our filth, our rebellion, so that all who repent and believe in Him would be clothed—not with animal skin—but with His righteousness. We were exposed by sin. We are covered by grace.

So if shame has been preaching to you lately, hear the better word of the Gospel: in Christ, your past is not the final garment on your life. Jesus covers what sin uncovered. Jesus restores what guilt tried to bury.

Come out of hiding.
Drop the fig leaves.
Let grace dress the wound.
“For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ” (Galatians 3:27).

This is our hope:
From Eden to Calvary, God is the One who covers sinners who cannot cover themselves.
And that is still true tonight.
